prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Columbus after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Columbus Ohio for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
Quick clarifying question before I give firm names: do you mean Columbus, Ohio (most likely), or Columbus, GA / MS / another Columbus? Also, how serious were the injuries (minor, moderate, severe/permanent), and do you already have an at-fault/other driver identified and insurance info? With that I’ll give a tailored list of local firms to call.

While you reply, here’s what I can do immediately and what to look for when choosing whom to call:

What I’ll provide once you confirm the Columbus you mean
- A short, prioritized list of 5–8 specific personal injury law firms/offices in that Columbus, with phone numbers and a one-line reason to call each (experience, trial record, focus on car crashes, client reviews, willingness to take serious cases, track record handling medical liens).
- A recommended order (e.g., call 3 firms right away) and which firm types are best depending on your case seriousness (local boutique trial firm vs. large national firm).

What to look for / ask on your first call
- Fee structure: Do they work on contingency (no upfront attorney fee; lawyer takes a percentage only if you recover)? Ask the percentage and whether costs are deducted before or after the attorney’s fee.
- Experience: How many years handling car-accident PI cases? How many cases taken to trial vs. settled?
- Who will handle the case: Will a partner handle it or a junior attorney/adjuster? Get names.
- Case results: Ask for examples of similar cases and outcomes (settlements/verdicts). Results vary, but this helps assess experience.
- Medical liens / treatment: Do they help arrange treatment and handle medical liens?
- Communication: How often will they update you and what is the best way to contact the person handling your case?
- Timeline & expectations: How long before they send demand/settlement talks or file suit?
- Conflicts & fees: Any other costs you might owe (filing fees, expert fees) and how those are handled.
- References / reviews: Ask whether you can see client testimonials or online reviews.

What to bring to the first appointment or phone consult
- Police report number (or copy), photos of the scene/vehicles/injuries, contact and insurance info of all parties, medical records or bills you already have, names of witnesses, notes about how injuries affect daily life, and any correspondence from insurance companies.

Immediate practical tips after a crash
- Don’t give a recorded statement to the other party’s insurer without consulting a lawyer.
- Keep medical treatment records and follow doctors’ orders—gaps in treatment can weaken a claim.
- Get copies of the police crash report and preserve photos.

If you confirm which Columbus and a bit about your injuries/insurance status, I’ll send a specific list of local firms to call and rank them for your situation.
